current.text: He moved from the Clippers to Detroit and is projected as the starting power forward, replacing Tobias Harris. The projected starters are Cunningham, Robinson, Thompson, Collins and Duren.
Detroit's power forward depth is weak, so he should play about 30 to 31 minutes, as Harris did, and may also get more usage.
Detroit used a deep 12 to 13 player rotation last season, which limited everyone's minutes.
He becomes a real category-league value if he plays 31 minutes.
Fine in rounds 9 to 10 in category leagues and a round or two later in points leagues. His Yahoo rank of 116 is fair, and his ESPN rank of 99 is a bit high.
He has little upside. He should beat last season's rank of about 120 but will not return to his prime level and is no longer a 20 and 10 player.
His free throws dropped from 85% to 77% last season for no clear reason. He averaged only five rebounds in 27 minutes but is usually about an eight-rebound player.
The experts call him a worse fit for Detroit than Tobias Harris and a real-life downgrade, because Detroit loses Harris's shot creation.
Detroit is projected to win 50 to 51 games and finish third or fourth in the East.
Detroit's playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games in weeks 19 to 21. The team has 15 back-to-backs, with no rest risks expected.
Detroit has no notable injuries before the season.

durable.text: An off-ball play finisher. He spaces the corners, cuts and has been a good offensive rebounder throughout his career.
He does not create his own shot and is a passive player.
He shoots a high FG% and good free throws on low volume. His FG% is his best category.
He shoots a good percentage from three (41% last season) but takes few threes, and his three-point shooting is streaky.
He rarely passes. Assists are his weakest category.
He is a weak defender, and his steals and blocks are modest, at about one block a game.
Detroit is built on defense, and the front office only wants enough offense.

note: Collins is an end-of-roster pick for us. Yahoo and ESPN average costs are 1.0 and 1.2 USD, values are 2 to 3 USD, and ranks are 99 to 112, well below the 7 USD he cost in our league last season. He has no weak category, so he fits any build as a high FG% big with solid points and rebounds. He brings little upside and few assists. Early in the season, check that he reaches 30 to 31 minutes in Detroit's deep rotation and that his rebounds return toward 7 to 8 a game. If both happen, he beats a 1 to 3 USD price.
